conviction_note: The evidence is balanced. The stock has de-rated hard into the print (-53% from the 2026-06-18 high of $746, about 15x NTM against 43x in June, -22% over 20 days, about -7% intraday on print day), and the company's own September commentary points to rising margins. Against that, it has sold off after three straight prints, including -13% on a beat with an above-consensus guide in August, the consensus already sits at the top of the guided range, and its own memory-cost headwind may slow December gross-margin expansion. abs_move 9.0 (implied 7.38%, baseline median 8.37%, plus a December guide that is the whole debate); p_up 48 because the reaction function has sold the last three beats. The findings sum to -0.5, close to the scaled -0.36.
bar: Company guide (2026-08-05 8-K ex.99.1): revenue $4.1B +/- $0.1B, non-GAAP GM 55-56%, EPS $4.00 +/- $0.15, ~388M shares (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000106040/000162828026053305/a4ex991-pressreleaseq426.htm). Consensus from two roughly agreeing sources: Visible Alpha EPS $4.11 / revenue $4.16B (AOL/Investopedia 2026-10-22, https://www.aol.com/articles/tech-slump-hits-memory-stocks-150000000.html), and Zacks/Investing EPS $4.08 / revenue $4.14B (https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/western-digital-faces-earnings-test-as-hdd-pricing-debate-looms-93CH-4966687). The consensus EPS is near the $4.15 top of the guide. No December-quarter consensus was found; that guide is what the stock trades on, and its bar is unsourced.
positioning_check: Short interest 18.29M shares = 4.90% of float, 2.5 days to cover, record date 2026-09-30, up 5.9% from 17.28M on 2026-09-15 (MarketBeat/FINRA, https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/WDC/short-interest/). Not a crowded short. Baseline skew is +11.14 vol points (25d put IV over call IV, 'downside paid'), put/call OI 0.63, ATM IV 125%, straddle 7.38%. Run-up -22.13% over 20 days and -1.62% over 5 days; spot $350.67 sealed intraday 2026-10-22 against a 10-21 close of $378.51, so the stock was down about 7% into the print. 53% below its 52-week high. Morgan Stanley calls itself an 'aggressive buyer' into the print; Wells Fargo says the selloff is overdone.

findings.finding: At Citi's TMT conference on 2026-09-09, mid-quarter, CFO Sennesael said 'gross margin will continue to increase at a pretty good pace'. He said price per TB rose 18-19% YoY last quarter (9% two quarters earlier) with 'still a little bit more room', that 'the vast majority of fiscal 2027 is under LTA', and that the 40TB ePMR ramp starts this quarter. The company is supply-gated ('revenue is gated by the amount I can supply'). That supports a Q1 at or above the $4.1B guide midpoint and a December guide with sequential GM expansion beyond the 55-56% Q1 guide. Consensus revenue ($4.14-4.16B) already sits above the midpoint, so the upside is in the December guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: August 2026: EPS $3.56 vs $3.29 and revenue $3.75B vs $3.69B, Q1 guide above consensus (EPS $3.85-4.15 vs $3.77), and the stock closed -13.03% (-18% intraday). April 2026 -0.69%, January 2026 -10.12%. The name has sold beat-and-raise three times running.
findings.why_not_priced: The transcript is public but predates the October sector selloff. Since then targets have been cut (MS $676->$643, Wells $730->$450, UBS $525->$470) and the multiple has compressed from 43x to about 15x NTM, which prices a cycle end. If the market held the CFO's 'GM keeps rising at a good pace' as the base case, the stock would not be 53% off its high with puts bid 11 vol points over calls.
findings.independence: Morgan Stanley industry checks (spot HDD 2-5x contract, about 400EB shortfall 2027-28, December guide above consensus expected), https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/morgan-stanley-cuts-western-digital-target-raises-seagate-amid-hdd-selloff-4960078. This shares the Citi document with the component-cost finding below; that finding is the offsetting reading of the same transcript.

findings.finding: The selloff into the print is multiple, not estimates. The stock is -53% from its 2026-06-18 record close of $746.23, -22% over 20 days and about -7% intraday on print day ($378.51 -> ~$350.7), and trades at about 15x NTM against 43x in June. Meanwhile EPS estimates rose 1.33% over 60 days and Morgan Stanley says its target cut reflects lower multiples, not lower earnings. Short interest is only 4.9% of float (2.5 days), so the drawdown is long liquidation rather than a crowded short, which leaves room for an in-line December guide to be bought.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last three prints (-13.0%, -0.7%, -10.1%) came with the stock near its highs. The five prints from October 2024 to October 2025 were all up (+1.2 to +10.2%), and those came from lower valuations. No print in the baseline came after a drawdown this deep.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the +11.1 vol-point put skew says the option market expects further downside. Why it may be wrong for this print: a 50% drawdown with estimates rising leaves the put bid as hedging demand from remaining longs rather than a short thesis (SI 4.9%). The 15x NTM multiple already discounts a pricing peak that the company's LTA coverage of FY27 makes hard to show inside one quarter. If the market held 'estimates intact' as the view, the multiple would not have halved in four months.
findings.independence: Estimate revisions +1.33% over 60 days (Zacks via Investing.com, https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/western-digital-faces-earnings-test-as-hdd-pricing-debate-looms-93CH-4966687); MS target-cut rationale 'lower valuation multiples ... not weaker earnings expectations' (https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/morgan-stanley-cuts-western-digital-target-raises-seagate-amid-hdd-selloff-4960078); short interest from https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/WDC/short-interest/.

findings.finding: The quarter's bar is already at the top of the guide. Consensus EPS of $4.08-4.11 sits against a guide of $4.00 +/- $0.15 (top $4.15), and revenue of $4.14-4.16B against $4.1B +/- $0.1B. This name has sold three straight prints, including August's beat with an above-consensus guide (-13.0%). A September-quarter beat is expected and is not enough; the stock needs a December guide well above the street.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: August 2026: EPS beat $0.27 (+8%) and revenue +1.6% with the guide above consensus, -13.03%. January 2026 -10.12%, April 2026 -0.69%. Opening Bell Daily notes the stock fell after each of its last 3 reports.
findings.why_not_priced: The reaction pattern is public, but the consensus drifting to the guide's top edge means a 'normal' WDC beat (about 1-2% revenue) is already the bar. The skew reflects some of this.
findings.independence: The company guide is from the 2026-08-05 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000106040/000162828026053305/a4ex991-pressreleaseq426.htm); the August reaction to a beat with an above-consensus guide is reported at https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/western-digital-tops-estimates-offers-204900191.html.

findings.finding: Toshiba plans to roughly double its AI data-center HDD capacity by fiscal 2027 (~JPY60bn, about $380M, in the Philippines; medium-term capacity-share goal about 30% from just over 10%), per Nikkei on 2026-10-02. That day WDC fell about 10%. UBS's Arcuri says hyperscalers plan to push as much volume as they can to Toshiba. The call will be asked whether this changes LTA pricing for 2029-31, which management said in August was still being negotiated.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Commentary-driven: the 2026-10-02 report alone moved WDC -10.2%. There is no prior print where competitor capacity was the question.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it is the main wire narrative for the October selloff. What remains is the management answer on LTA pricing. If the market had fully absorbed it, UBS and Wells would not still be framing customer-contract talks as the open question for the call.
findings.independence: Analysis noting the plan names no customer commitments (https://letsdatascience.com/news/toshiba-plans-to-double-hdd-capacity-for-ai-data-centers-3b445b0f) cuts the other way; Wells Fargo calls the concern 'misunderstood' (https://finance.biggo.com/news/2fa93fdb-e4c6-4ef2-b9c6-cf4f433f2c80). Sized small for that reason.

findings.finding: Gross-margin expansion is decelerating. The Q1 GM guide of 55-56% is only +60 to +160bp over Q4's 54.4%, against +390bp from Q3 (50.5%) to Q4. At Citi the CFO said DRAM and NAND input costs are a headwind to cost-per-TB declines and that WDC is 'in between two product transitions' (40TB ePMR ramping, HAMR not until 1H CY27). Memory prices kept rising: TrendForce saw DRAM contract +13-18% in Jul-Sep, and Micron guided its November quarter to $61.5B against $57.0B consensus on 2026-09-30. That raises the risk of a modest December GM guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: August 2026: the Q1 GM guide implied a sharply slower margin step-up, and the stock fell -13% despite the beat. The baseline does not isolate which line drove it.
findings.why_not_priced: The pricing narrative dominates previews; only one preview (Investing.com, 2026-10-22) mentions component inflation, and none quantifies it. If it were priced, the December GM consensus (FY27 GM about 57.6% per data providers) would sit below the CFO's 'pretty good pace'.
findings.independence: Micron's FQ4 2026 results and guide (https://beancount.io/de/blog/2026/10/02/micron-fy2026-q4-earnings-analysis). The Investing.com preview flags component costs and mix pressuring margins (https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/western-digital-faces-earnings-test-as-hdd-pricing-debate-looms-93CH-4966687). It shares the Citi transcript with finding 1. Memory-to-HDD-cost transmission is a proxy beyond the company's own qualitative remark.

findings.finding: Convertible cleanup. On 2026-08-26 WDC exchanged about $191.0M of its 3.00% 2028 converts for ~$192.7M cash plus shares. On 2026-09-14 it called the remaining $109.5M for redemption on 2026-11-16: conversion deadline 2026-11-12, 26.5231 shares per $1,000, principal in cash, the excess in stock over a 40-day averaging period. That is about 2.6M shares, roughly 0.7% of the ~388M share count. The balance sheet is net cash after the Sandisk stake monetization. The money retires debt and funds nothing new, and there is no distress signal; the sign is neutral.
findings.why_not_priced: It is small and public. The dilution is likely inside the guided ~388M diluted share count, and conversion-arb hedge selling during averaging is modest relative to 9M shares a day.

findings.finding: AI-infrastructure memory and storage demand was confirmed after WDC last spoke. On 2026-09-30 Micron beat its own FQ4 guide (revenue $54.23B vs $50B +/- $1B) and guided FQ1 FY27 to $61.5B +/- $1.5B against $57.0B consensus. That undercuts the 'AI financing' fear that the October 22 tape is blaming for the memory/storage selloff.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No baseline line; peer read-through. Micron itself moved only about +1.5% after hours on the report.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. HDD and memory stocks sold off after it anyway (WDC -10% on 10-02, DRAM ETF -5% on 10-22), so the market is discounting financing risk rather than current demand. The residual is whether WDC's December guide confirms demand.
findings.independence: Proxy: a peer in an adjacent market, not WDC's own number. The same Micron document is used in finding 5 as a cost signal; here it is read as a demand signal, which is a different line.

findings.finding: Morgan Stanley's industry checks (around 2026-10-20) find spot HDD transactions at 2-5x contracted prices and a possible ~400EB supply shortfall in 2027-28. MS forecasts WDC about 10% above consensus and expects a December guide above expectations. Most of FY27 is under LTA (per the CFO), so spot strength mostly does not flow to WDC this year; it bears on the LTA renewal tone.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Analyst checks have not protected the last three prints: MS was Overweight through the -13% August reaction.
findings.source_date: 2026-10-20 (approximate; article cites MS note ahead of the 10-22 print)
findings.why_not_priced: It is on the wire, so mostly priced. The stock fell further after the note (about -7% on 10-22), so the market is not crediting the checks.
findings.independence: The CFO's 'still a little bit more room' on price per TB (Citi, 2026-09-09) points the same way but is weaker. It shares no document with the other findings except as context for finding 1.

baseline_tension: Findings 2 (washed-out multiple), 1, 7 and 8 lean long against the +11 vol-point put skew and the -22% run-up; findings 3, 4 and 5 agree with the skew. Net they offset, and the reaction function (three straight beats sold) tips p_up just below 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): finding 1 (CFO margin commentary) cut from +1.0 to +0.7 because this name has sold three straight beat-and-raise prints; p_up moved from 50 to 48.

Lesson 7 (sign against a strong skew): finding 2 (washed-out positioning) cut from +1.0 to +0.7. Kept positive with an explicit reason: short interest is only 4.9%, so the put bid is hedging, and estimates are rising while the multiple compresses.

Lessons 3 and 5: findings 1 and 5 share the Citi transcript, and findings 5 and 7 share the Micron document on different lines (cost vs demand); stated in independence. Proxies (Micron, MS checks) left small and not unfiled.
Lesson 6: Seagate's print and the convert settlement moved to outside_window. The December-quarter bar is unsourced, which caps the guidance findings at small sizes.
Lesson 4: the convert exchange and redemption were checked against what the money buys (debt retirement, net-cash balance sheet) and signed neutral.
